messages:
kevin: Swarm for ACME POC. Their Windows app (enterprise image) shows streaming responses stall after 5-30s and client logs show intermittent 407 Proxy Authentication Required. Looks specific to hosts using WinHTTP/IE system proxy. @samir can you own?

acme_netops: Confirmed: proxy is Microsoft ISA/Appliance doing NTLM/Negotiate. App uses system proxy and we see NTLM handshakes in proxy logs. Sometimes initial CONNECT completes but chunked stream is buffered then closed.

samir: Two things to clarify: 1) which SDK versions + transport (fetch/node http/requests)? 2) are users behind Azure AD SSO/NTLM only or is there a gateway that can do pass-through?

acme_netops: Node clients run @redwood/js 1.5.0 via electron wrapper (uses node-fetch under the hood). Python clients on endpoints use redwood-client 1.0.3 via requests. Both go through corporate proxy using machine account NTLM.

izzy: NTLM is stateful and many proxies buffer chunked responses until body complete, which breaks streaming. Also NTLM adds extra roundtrips for auth which can confuse connection pooling. Quick options:
- Bypass proxy for api.redwood.ai if allowed (NO_PROXY).
- Use an outbound tunnel (corporate SOCKS or SSH jump) that converts to plain TLS to API.
- Use a local NTLM auth proxy like cntlm/ntlmaps on the host that handles NTLM and speaks plain HTTP upstream.

frank: SDK-level mitigations we can ship: enable persistent keep-alive agents by default for Node when HTTP_PROXY is set; expose a fetch/agent override in the SDK so customers can pass https-proxy-agent with { keepAlive: true }. For Python, document requests-ntlm integration and recommend session.mount + larger pool sizes.

samir: Workaround repro snippets for ACME to try:
Node + https-proxy-agent:
```js
const HttpsProxyAgent = require('https-proxy-agent');
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent({ host: 'proxy.corp', port: 8080, keepAlive: true });
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.KEY, fetchOptions: { agent, timeout: 180000 } });
await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-big', stream: true });
```
Python + cntlm local proxy:
```py
# run cntlm on localhost:3128 (auth handled locally)
proxies = { 'http': 'http://127.0.0.1:3128', 'https': 'http://127.0.0.1:3128' }
s = requests.Session()
s.proxies.update(proxies)
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_maxsize=100))
resp = s.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json=payload, timeout=(5,180))
```
These avoid passing NTLM through to the upstream TLS connection.

acme_netops: We can stand up cntlm on a test host. Will try and report.

izzy: Additional diagnostic asks:
- tcpdump (or Wireshark) capture showing the CONNECT + post-CONNECT TLS bytes for failed stream.
- proxy logs for timestamps of failed streams (showing 407 or buffer/close).
- Node debug logs: set NODE_DEBUG=request,net and paste.

frank: I can prototype a small SDK flag `forceProxyTunnel: true` that will prefer opening raw CONNECT tunnels and proactively re-auth on 407, plus a streaming-start retry (one immediate retry) for ECONNRESET/EOF. ETA: 6 hours for a PR and test.

salesops-bot: POC details: hosted=true, dedicated=false, account=poc-ACME-77, current rps=50, burst=100.

kevin: Great. Action items: 1) ACME: run cntlm test + tcpdump + proxy logs and post results here. 2) Frank: prototype `forceProxyTunnel` toggle + streaming-start retry PR (ETA ~6h). 3) Izzy: doc PR on Python NTLM best practices and sample cntlm config. 4) Samir: offer screenshare if cntlm test fails.

acme_netops: We'll run tests and upload logs later today. Thanks for the clear steps.

kevin: Closing swarm for now; please tag me in updates so I can update AE.
